clue.text: Lack in desert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noun for a shortcoming or flaw
second meaning: a verb for abandoning one's side or country

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shortage in an arid region; 'desert' is really the verb, stressed on its second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault or deficiency, and to defect is to abandon allegiance and go over to the other side.

clue.text: Party member in protest meeting about blackleg

parts.note: a demo is a protest demonstration
C is short for circa, about
a rat is a strikebreaker or traitor

explanation.surface: A party activist turns up at a protest rally about a strikebreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is a British term for a worker who crosses a picket line; 'rat' carries the same sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the US Democratic Party, or more loosely any party supporting democracy.

clue.text: In favour of church's influence

parts.note: for means supporting or in favour of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone supports the church having a say in public affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Force can mean power or sway over events, as in being a force for good, which is influence.

clue.text: Collier — heartless one, man due for retraining

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is taken out of the word
retraining reshapes something into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the one just named, a collier, minus its central letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A collier, a ruthless fellow, is due to be retrained for a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the defined word, so the collier itself, heartless, joins MAN to be mixed. Collier is British for a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a worker in a coal mine; the word comes from coal, and it also names a coal ship.

clue.text: One who's worked with mummy?

parts.note: surface reading: someone who has worked alongside their mother
setter's reading: an Egyptian preserved corpse, and the person who prepared it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mummy' reads as a British word for mother, so this sounds like a child helping out in the family business; the mummy is really the preserved dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians preserved corpses with resins and wrappings, and the specialist who did that preserving work made the mummy.

clue.text: Flowering plant, mystical for a few nomads

indicators.note: something mystical is strange and transformed, so the letters are changed in order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A flowering plant is said to hold mystical meaning for a few wandering tribespeople.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadow saffron is Colchicum autumnale, a crocus-like autumn-flowering plant also called autumn crocus.

clue.text: Leading Greek character in local pharmacy

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across the gap

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A prominent Greek figure works at the neighbourhood chemist's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading Greek character' sounds like an important person; it is the first letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it leads all the other letters.

clue.text: Head of family in secret society cut during procession

indicators.note: cutting trims something short, so the word loses its final letter
during places one thing in the middle of another, enclosed by it

parts.note: a march is a procession
a triad is a Chinese secret society; here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A family's head belongs to a secret society that has been cut short during a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A triad is a Chinese criminal secret society; 'cut' docks its tail before it goes inside the procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who rules a family or clan, its female head.

clue.text: Become less severe about period of self-denial

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone eases up on their Lenten fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften one's harsh attitude and give way, so it means to become more lenient.

clue.text: Spanish girl in Caribbean island

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Spanish woman's name
second meaning: Isla ..., a Venezuelan island in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl is staying on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a common Spanish given name, and it is also the name of a large Venezuelan holiday island.

clue.text: Tending aralia? Unlikely here at Blenheim Palace, say

indicators.note: unlikely suggests an improbable form, so the letters land in an odd new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A visitor doubts anyone grows aralia shrubs in the grounds of Blenheim Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is a stately home in Oxfordshire, England, with formal gardens; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Blenheim Palace has a formal Italian Garden, an example of the terraced, statue-filled style found at grand houses.

clue.text: Floral feature in ring worn by tenor

indicators.note: something worn is carried around something else, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A floral motif appears on a ring worn by a tenor singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery but is the sound of bells; PE(T)AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured leaf-like parts of a flower, an obvious feature of any bloom.

clue.text: Stuff round end of meringue?

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of meringue

explanation.surface: A cook asks what to pile around the tip of a meringue.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the filling piped around a meringue, so it is the definition as well as the wordplay; the question mark flags that double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Whipped cream is the usual filling stuffed around and between meringues in desserts like pavlova or Eton mess.

clue.text: Esteem shown in a piece of direct speech

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a piece is a small part, here just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of direct
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Respect is expressed in a frank, direct speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direct speech' looks like the grammar term, but 'direct' only lends one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and respect, a stronger form of high regard or esteem.

clue.text: Men, losing face, caught by artful chap with sniffer dog

indicators.note: the face is the front, so the word loses its opening letter
artful suggests crafty manipulation, so the letters are cunningly rearranged

parts.note: the word men without its first letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men are nabbed by a crafty fellow who has a sniffer dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' just places EN among the other letters before the whole lot is mixed. 'Sniffer dog' looks like one unit; 'dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The affenpinscher is a small German toy breed of dog with a monkey-like face.

clue.text: Provided suitable solicitor to ring editor

parts.note: fit means suitable

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits custom
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A firm supplied a fitting lawyer to phone the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT + TO(ED)UT. 'Solicitor' looks like a British lawyer, but it is one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fitted out is to be equipped or supplied with what is needed, so it means provided.

clue.text: Leader's sharp gaining initial advantage

parts.note: a head is a leader; with the apostrophe s
tart means sharp in taste

explanation.surface: A leader's keen mind wins them an early lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A head start is an advantage given or gained at the beginning of a race or contest.

clue.text: Offer to support old girl

parts.note: a prop is a support
O is an abbreviation for old
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: An offer is made to help an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old girl' reads as one phrase for an older woman, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for consideration, such as an offer of marriage or a business plan.

clue.text: Punish errant fathead cruelly

indicators.note: treating something cruelly roughs it up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: Someone urges harsh punishment for a wayward idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Coating someone in hot tar and feathers was a mob punishment, and the phrase now means to punish or humiliate severely.

clue.text: Become more communicative, ring writer at university

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
a pen is a writing instrument
in British usage one is 'up' at university while in residence

explanation.surface: A student writer finally starts talking openly, and gives a friend a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to start talking freely about one's feelings, being less reserved.

clue.text: Extinct reptile and raptor, last to survive us possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of survive
taken as written

explanation.surface: An extinct reptile and a bird of prey; which of them might outlive us?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raptor' sits beside 'extinct reptile' as if it were a dinosaur, but it is only letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Pterosaurs were flying reptiles of the dinosaur age that died out about 66 million years ago.

clue.text: Loire's seen vaguely from bay window

indicators.note: something seen vaguely looks blurred and jumbled, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: the French river's letters, to be mixed

explanation.surface: The river Loire glimpsed hazily from a bay window of a chateau.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is an upper-storey window that projects out from a wall, a kind of bay window.

clue.text: Latest of journalists to pen an exclusive

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of journalists
a pen for animals, such as a hen coop

explanation.surface: The newest reporters are told to write up an exclusive story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' reads as the verb to write, but it is the noun for an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is a news story one paper publishes before its rivals, which is what an exclusive is.

clue.text: Old boy, priest, is showing signs

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, a former pupil
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A former pupil, now a priest, is displaying symptoms.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is a crossword favourite for priest, from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped marks used in print to flag footnotes or doubtful passages, so they are signs.

clue.text: I complain about Ruth's mother-in-law

indicators.note: turning about faces the other way, so the words are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the mother-in-law of a woman called Ruth.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Book of Ruth, Naomi is the mother of Ruth's husband, and Ruth follows her to Bethlehem.

clue.text: Droppings are found at end of the Square — overalls required

parts.note: dung is animal droppings
taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Pigeon droppings at the far side of the town square mean overalls are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Square' looks like a named place, but 'the' gives one letter and 'Square' another.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing trousers with a bib and shoulder straps, a type of work overalls.

clue.text: Hemp, perhaps?

parts.note: surface reading: an example of a fibre crop
setter's reading: cannabis, the plant that gives the drug known as pot

explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense is a houseplant grown in a container; here 'pot' is slang for cannabis, and hemp is that plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemp is the cannabis plant, the source of the drug called pot, so it is literally a plant of pot.

clue.text: When one chooses to use a plough round onset of winter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to till is to plough land

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of winter

explanation.surface: A farmer may choose when to plough, even as winter sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: A + T(W)ILL; the 'a' looks part of 'a plough', but it stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever one likes, freely and as one chooses.
